clue.text: Boy with great expectations owed extraordinary unknown quantity, shut up

parts.note: Pip is the boy hero of Dickens's novel Great Expectations

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual order, so the letters of owed are rearranged

parts.note: in algebra n stands for an unknown number

explanation.surface: A Dickensian lad who owes a strange sum is told to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal phrasal verbs for falling silent or stopping talking.

clue.text: Struggle to overtake backmarkers in particular, hungry for some pie!

parts.note: to puff is to breathe hard while struggling with effort
to overtake is to go past

indicators.note: backmarkers are those at the rear, so the last letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A runner struggles past the back of the field, desperate for pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Light flaky layered dough is used to make many pies.

clue.text: Still sexy, old fruit having bottom wiped in pub

indicators.note: in means the other pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
hot means sexy

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is removed from the fruit

parts.note: a grape is a fruit

explanation.surface: An attractive old friend is still sitting in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAPE loses its E. 'Still' looks like an adverb, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single static image, as opposed to moving film.

clue.text: Base lifted, little word from caveman having to fix a computer

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a flower bed
ug is the grunt cartoon cavemen are given

explanation.surface: A caveman struggles to get his computer working.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove the errors or bugs from a program or machine is to repair it.

clue.text: Satellite dish under woodwork for starters, possibly in a good position

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way
for starters means the first letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A satellite dish fixed under the woodwork might be well placed.
explanation.walkthrough: SATELLITE plus D, U and W are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-placed house or business is conveniently located.

clue.text: Reportedly spotted a hairy thing

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by how they are said rather than spelt

parts.note: spotted means spied; said with a non-rhotic accent 'spied a' rhymes with the answer

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have seen something hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech the final R is silent, so 'spied a' and the eight-legged creature sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarantulas and many other arachnids have bristly legs and bodies, a loose cryptic description of the creature.

clue.text: Dynamic Duo seen with person, slow and clumsy

indicators.note: dynamic suggests energetic movement, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A superhero pair with a sidekick move slowly and awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic Duo' looks like Batman and Robin, but Dynamic is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, lumbering movement or style is ungainly and laboured.

clue.text: See 26
One necked by an Elizabethan that's uncultured, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: rough means coarse or unrefined

explanation.surface: A Tudor courtier wears something that sounds rather coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necked' is a playful verb: worn around the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleated starched collar was worn around the throat in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Junket by Labour leader and shadow chancellor in shorts and shirt, sportingly

indicators.note: by means beside, so the junket is placed next to the two politicians

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
Ed Balls was Labour's shadow chancellor of the exchequer when this puzzle appeared
a junket is a pleasure trip, often at public expense

explanation.surface: Two Labour politicians go on a jolly dressed in sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls in a different place: FOOT BALLS TRIP is read as FOOTBALL STRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's matching kit of shirt and shorts is called its strip in Britain.

clue.text: Those helping young people in bureau, nice folk

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Nice people in an office are the ones helping the young.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Children's Fund works for children's welfare worldwide.

clue.text: Hollywood legend having come round dined on top of tall furniture item

indicators.note: having come round means the star's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood star
to dine is to eat; ate is its past tense
on and leg are the same side of the field in cricket

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of tall

explanation.surface: A film star comes round for dinner and eats off a tall table.
explanation.walkthrough: A gateleg table has hinged legs that swing out like gates to hold up its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of table with drop leaves, a household piece.

clue.text: Cut around lakes with hard blade on the farm

indicators.note: around tells us the word for cut wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
loughs are lakes in Ireland
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a blade for farm use near some lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The share is the cutting blade of a plough used in fields.

clue.text: Ability to recover home without deposit initially left one to invest

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the pieces go inside
without means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a residence is a home

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of deposit

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone recovers after leaving a home without paying a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIDENCE loses D to give RESIENCE, which takes L and I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughness or the capacity to bounce back after a setback.

clue.text: Value fuse, unless blown

indicators.note: a blown fuse has burst, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A fuse is only worth something unless it has blown.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility and worth are near synonyms for practical merit.

clue.text: See 9
23 24 in this event is logical, not entirely in the pink

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the colour

parts.note: puce is a pinkish-purple colour
taken as written

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sane means rational and sensible

explanation.surface: Someone claims a revolution in this contest is perfectly sensible but not quite healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: SANE loses its E. The cross-reference read as two words gives an Arab horse that springs, a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a show-jumping competition over very high walls, where a horse leaps.

clue.text: See 21
Still awaiting salesman to collect one carbon copy

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative

indicators.note: to collect means the word for still awaiting gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: someone still awaited has not arrived yet, so is late
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A salesman is waiting for a carbon copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copy' looks like the definition as one phrase, but carbon gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something exactly is to duplicate it.

clue.text: Body suits the wrong way round, facing initially to the rear

indicators.note: to the rear tells us the next piece goes at the end
the wrong way round means the word for suits is read backwards

parts.note: suits means fits, as clothes fit a person

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of facing is taken

explanation.surface: A tailor complains suits are back to front with the facing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Spin round gradually at first, following someone in restaurant, alluring type

indicators.note: round means the word for spin goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to swirl is to spin round

indicators.note: following means the first letter comes after the diner

parts.note: a diner in a restaurant is an eater

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of gradually is taken

explanation.surface: A diner slowly spins round in a restaurant, attracting attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweater girl was a 1940s-50s term for a pin-up who wore tight jumpers (sweaters).
explanation.definitionFit: Such a woman was a glamorous pin-up, an attractive figure.

parts.note: the cross-reference read as a comic strip about the sport, a long-running British comic

explanation.definitionFit: This British comic about a footballer ran as a strip cartoon for decades.

clue.text: Old leader gets around houses

indicators.note: houses means the words contain the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A former ruler visits many homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian emperors were ruling monarchs before the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Modern revolution grips Bahrain, internationally hated leaders getting ousted all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered and rearranged
leaders are first letters, here of internationally and hated, which are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: An uprising takes hold in Bahrain, its hated rulers deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIPS BAHRAIN without I and H is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2010-12 uprisings across the Middle East and North Africa were a recent political upheaval.

clue.text: See 23
Temporary suspension gives a diva a change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter of the singer's name is replaced

parts.note: Beyoncé is a famous pop diva
taken as written, the replacement letter

explanation.surface: A singer has a change of heart and things are put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle O of BEYONCE becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in abeyance is suspended for the time being, in a state of dormancy.

clue.text: One causing friction with sweetheart, finds plaything all soaped up?

parts.note: someone who rubs things creates friction
duck is an affectionate form of address in parts of Britain, like love or dear

explanation.surface: A troublemaker with a lover finds a toy covered in soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow bath toy that floats in sudsy water is a familiar child's plaything.

clue.text: Generous society lacking cobblers?

parts.note: in the fairy tale The Elves and the Shoemaker, elves make shoes overnight
less means without, as in 'penniless'

explanation.surface: A society with no shoemakers might ask if it is generous.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers is a British slang word for nonsense, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts others first is unselfish and giving.
